Get the Health Insurance Premium Regions

Source: R/praemienregion.R
praemienregion.Rd

Returns the assignment of municipalities to the premium regions of the mandatory health insurance for a premium year, as published by the Federal Office of Public Health (BAG) on priminfo.admin.ch. Premiums differ between up to three regions within a canton, so the region is needed to compare premiums or claims across municipalities, and to map the regions with combineRegions().

Usage

praemienregion(
  year = NULL,
  output = c("gemeinde", "ortschaft"),
  cache = TRUE,
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

year

premium year; the default NULL uses the current year.

output

"gemeinde" for one row per municipality and region, or "ortschaft" for the rows as delivered (one per postcode and locality).

cache

logical; if TRUE, results are read from and written to the local cache (see cacheList()).

refresh

logical; if TRUE, the source is queried again even if a cached copy exists.

Value

For output = "gemeinde", a data.frame with the columns jahr_n, gem_id, gem_x, kanton_c, preg_c (region within the canton, 0 to 3), preg_x (e.g. "ZH3") and split_l; the key is jahr_n + gem_id + preg_c. For output = "ortschaft", the columns plz_n and ort_x are added and split_l is dropped.

Details

The regions are defined in the ordinance of the EDI, which remains the binding source; the files on priminfo are its machine-readable companion and are available from 2004. Cantons without regional differentiation have region 0. The file of a year lists the municipalities and localities valid in that year; join it with municipality data of the same stand.

The data are read from the sheet A_COM of the file (other sheets hold information and mutations). Columns are found by their headers (BFS number, region, canton, municipality, postcode, locality), not by position; a change of the layout is an error naming the headers found. Where the regions follow locality rather than municipality boundaries, a municipality can lie in two regions; it then appears once per region with split_l = TRUE.

See also

combineRegions() to draw the regions.

Other swiss.register: gemeinde(), gemeindeMutationen(), kanton(), raumgliederung()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
preg <- praemienregion(2026)
table(preg$preg_x[preg$kanton_c == "ZH"])
} # }
